necessary_context.content: z*(x)=argmin over z in R^p of G(z,x), h(x)=F(z*(x),x), x in R^d. Algorithm sections use F=(1/m)sum_j F_j and G=(1/n)sum_i G_i, with positive integer m,n.
necessary_context.name: Bilevel objective and finite sums

necessary_context.content: grad_1 is the z gradient, grad_2 the x gradient, G_11 is p by p, G_21 is d by p. v*(x)=-G_11(z*(x),x)^(-1)grad_1 F(z*(x),x); grad h(x)=grad_2 F(z*(x),x)+G_21(z*(x),x)v*(x). Vector norm is Euclidean; matrix norm is spectral.
necessary_context.name: Derivative orientation and exact auxiliary state

necessary_context.content: Dz=grad_1 G; Dv=G_11 v+grad_1 F; Dx=G_21 v+grad_2 F. SOBA and SABA estimate these directions. Away from the exact inner and auxiliary states, unbiasedness for Dx does not assert unbiasedness for grad h.
necessary_context.name: Exact directions versus stochastic directions

necessary_context.applies_to: Interpretation of lemma regularity; no convergence-rate claim
necessary_context.content: Proposition 2.1 explicitly assumes G(.,x) strongly convex for every x. Section 3 later states Assumption 3.1: F twice differentiable with Lipschitz gradient and Hessian; Assumption 3.2: G three times continuously differentiable, uniformly mu_G-strongly convex in z, with Lipschitz first through third derivatives. The reconstructed lemma explicitly states sufficient C1/C2 regularity rather than silently importing all rate-analysis hypotheses.
necessary_context.name: Regularity context
